body.statement:
Using the second-order staircase alignment handle, derive a primitive block-ratio expression \(\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\) and constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), common across \(n\), such that
\[
 c\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\le\Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)
 \le C\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)
\]
for every vanishing tail sequence \(\eta_n\), where \(\Delta_n^*\) is optimized over the explicitly defined slice \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}\) of the baseline event-transfer class \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\).  Establish the conditional coverage frontier in this finite-slice experiment: if there is a deterministic \(h_n\downarrow0\) such that
\[
 \sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}
 P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h_n)^c\}\to0,
 \qquad h_n\log^2(4K)\to0,
\]
then \(\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\to0\) must imply \(\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}\Gamma_n(P_n)\to0\).  Conversely, for every primitive candidate \(\beta\) with \(\beta\triangleleft\Delta^{\dagger}\) and \(\beta_n(K)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\to0\) along a subsequence on which \(\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\) is bounded away from zero, construct one complete staggered low-rank triangular array
\[
 (P_n)_{n\ge1}\in\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,com}}
 \subseteq\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\cap\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,pub}}
\]
such that \(P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}\), \(\delta_n(P_n;\eta_n)\ge c\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\), \(\liminf_n\Gamma_n(P_n)>0\), and, for some deterministic \(h_n\downarrow0\),
\[
 P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h_n)^c\}\to0,
 \qquad h_n\log^2(4K)\to0.
\]
The derivation must first test whether the balanced strong-factor rank-one second-order remainder is \(o(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\); if so, \(\Delta^{\dagger}\) must use the smaller attained scale.  The common-subclass and score-stability restrictions apply only to the converse witness and do not assume any remainder lower bound.

obligation.what_is_open: The exact second-order Choi--Yuan remainder on a balanced rank-one complete array in the common subclass, a matching lower bound for its \(1-\eta_n\) quantile with signs aligned across horizons, and preservation of the displayed feasible score-stability rate on that witness.
obligation.obstruction: The published \(R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\) is an upper perturbation envelope, not an attained expansion.  The frozen estimator definition omits the nuclear-norm objective's tuning sequence, KKT solution map, exact debiasing formula, and growing rowwise loading control needed to compute the mandated second-order term and certify the witness's score stability.  The common-subclass repair strengthens legality but supplies none of those missing estimator identities.
obligation.attempted: The balanced rank-one coefficient calculation determines only the first-order score and its shared-cell covariance.  The generic transfer proves sufficiency for any attained modulus \(u_n\), and the Choi--Yuan block result gives a one-sided event implication, but successive norm inequalities provide neither a reverse bound nor a sign-controlled undercoverage array.  The published-only approximate-rank witness cannot be used because the directive correctly requires the converse inside the common exact-rank subclass.
obligation.partial_result:
The definitions identify the exact but nonprimitive event-transfer frontier:
\[
 \Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)
 =\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}
 \inf\{d\ge0:P_n(\|\rho_n\|_\infty>d)\le\eta_n\}.
\]
The generic transfer theorem proves that any deterministic \(u_n\) satisfying
\[
 \sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}
 P_n\{\|\rho_n\|_\infty>u_n\}\le\eta_n
\]
is a sufficient simultaneous remainder modulus, subject separately to the displayed score-stability probabilities.  The Choi--Yuan specialization gives the computable implication
\[
 \mathcal A_n(C)\subseteq
 \{\|\rho_n\|_\infty\le C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\}.
\]
Thus, if the unsimplified simultaneous block-failure probability were uniformly at most \(\eta_n\), one would obtain the one-sided bound \(\Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)\le C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\).  No reverse inequality follows.  The class-comparison proposition additionally proves that a future lower witness constructed in \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,com}}\) is automatically legal for both the baseline event-transfer experiment and the published approximate-rank class, so its converse transfers upward.

More precisely, if the requested upper equivalence \(\Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)\le C\Delta_n^\dagger(K;\eta_n)\) were established, then the definition of the infimum implies
\[
 \sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}
 P_n\{\|\rho_n\|_\infty>(C+1)\Delta_n^\dagger(K;\eta_n)\}
 \le\eta_n. \tag{1}
\]
Indeed, for each law the infimum is at most \(C\Delta_n^\dagger\), so some admissible threshold lies strictly below \((C+1)\Delta_n^\dagger\), and the tail probability is nonincreasing in the threshold.  Under the score-stability conditions displayed in the narrowed question, apply the generic theorem with \(u_n=(C+1)\Delta_n^\dagger(K;\eta_n)\).  The corrected cell-leverage envelope bounds its Gaussian term by \(C(\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm{lev}})^{1/4}\), equation (1) bounds the remainder-event failure by \(\eta_n\), and all other displayed terms vanish.  Therefore
\[
 \Delta_n^\dagger(K;\eta_n)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\to0
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}\Gamma_n(P_n)\to0
\]
under that score-stability condition.  Thus the narrowed upper transfer is reduced completely to the requested primitive upper equivalence; the unresolved content is its primitive evaluation and the score-stable common-subclass lower witness.

body.justification: The remaining question is the attained second-order scale on a legal common-subclass array, not the sufficiency of a published norm envelope.
body.gap: The frozen estimator does not expose the KKT and debiasing map needed to calculate and align the second-order remainder or the growing rowwise loading rate needed to keep a converse witness score-stable, so no primitive two-sided frontier is proved.
body.consumer: Resolving the narrowed question would determine whether any weaker simultaneous-band envelope fails on both the event-transfer and published domains.
